verdict.rationale: Glama is an MCP gateway and hosting platform, so per-end-user credential isolation is a fair question to ask of it. The pack, however, only shows generic gateway credential management and per-tool enable/disable controls. Nothing documents separate connected accounts or scoped tokens per end user of a customer's product, so these adjacent controls earn no credit.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can maintain separate connected accounts and scoped tokens per end user of my product, so each user's agent acts only on that user's credentials
